evidence.clarity: 1440: H1 'Heat water when power is cheap. Have it hot when you need it.' plus lede 'a controller your electrician adds to the electric water heater you already have' says what and for whom; the headline alone is benefit-generic, so the product noun only arrives in the lede. Primary button 'Join the install list' names its object.
evidence.fit: Example strip is labelled ('Example tariff', 'There is no savings figure on this page'); no savings number anywhere; separate 'For electricians' spec list and 'For utility programmes' section; form says up front 'there is no list server yet... not sent anywhere'; unnamed pilot and in-progress listing stated. Electrician path is a spec table plus a button, utility path is four prose blocks with no artifact of its own; 'Join as an electrician' (1440, clicked) scrolls to #join but leaves role on 'A homeowner'.
evidence.distinctiveness: The 24-cell hour strip with water-drop toggles, red/blue tariff band and stepped tank-level bars is a real product idea. The rest of the page is a familiar stack: centred-left text hero with empty right half, two-column prose grids for How it works and Utilities, a 'Where we stand' status table. Without the strip it would read as a tidy generic template.
evidence.proof: Strip is operable and consistent: 1440 default shows standard heater at 6,7,8,20 vs Tankshift moved to 4,5,6,15; readout Peak 1/0. Tapping hour 18 switched usage to 'Custom (tap the strip)' and readout to Peak 2/0. But at 1440 only the strip's top rows peek in at y~730-900 and at 390 it starts below the first screen (~y 1000).
evidence.craft: Consistent condensed sans headings with serif body, even section rhythm, readable table. Defects: 1440 first screen has a large dead right half beside the text-only hero; 1440 with many draws the controls row leaves a tall empty block under the selects beside the readout; 768 the strip's final 'Shoulder' band label is cropped at the right edge; band labels are dropped on short bands (two-peaks tariff shows an unlabelled grey and blue block at 20-24).
evidence.mobile: 390: no menu, the nav wraps into two lines that eat ~160px of the first screen; CTAs visible, strip not. Strip scrolls sideways inside its container with fixed row labels and a 'Swipe the strip sideways' note (no page overflow), but hour toggles measured 21x40px (19x40 at 768), well under 44px. After tapping a cell, the readout table sits below two selects and the tank radios, out of view. 320: CTA falls below the first screen.
evidence.honesty: Example labelled where it appears ('on an example tariff', 'This is a simplified example... not what you would pay'), form states before submit that nothing is sent, and success reads 'You're on the list on this device... Nothing was sent'. Status table is candid. Small stretch: 'It learns when the house uses hot water' describes behaviour the brief does not state.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440/768/390: tariff select (3 options), usage select, tank-size radios, 24 hour toggles (aria-pressed buttons). Empty state: cleared all four draws -> 'No hot water used, so no heating.' and readout prompt 'Tap an hour on the strip...'. Heavy load (17 draws, small tank) -> note explains peak heating still lands. Form: empty submit shows per-field error under Postcode; bad email shows email error; valid submit shows done panel with summary; 'Change my entry' restores postcode and role. No console errors. Feedback on mobile lands below the fold of where you tapped.
evidence.copy: Plain, specific and in the customer's words: 'so the tank is hot at seven in the morning and the bill is not', 'Plumbing: None. No mixing valve, no new tank', 'Override: A boost control on the unit heats now, for the odd day with visitors'. A few soft spots: 'the list is told before anyone else' is awkward, 'The honest version, kept current' is self-congratulatory, and utility copy is general ('Shifting you can count').
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific promise and right action, with only the top edge of the strip (ruler, tariff band, drops) visible at the bottom; nothing in view shows the shift happening yet. 390: headline, lede and both buttons visible but no artifact or example in view, and the two-line nav pushes the H1 to y=199.

problems: The artifact is not in the first screen at 390 and barely at 1440; the hero is a text block with a dead right half, so the page's best idea is held back
Mobile hour toggles are ~21px wide and the readout that answers a tap sits several hundred px below the strip; nav has no menu and wraps to two lines
Outside the strip the structure is generic (prose grids, status table); the utility audience gets no artifact and 'Join as an electrician' does not preselect the electrician role

evidence.clarity: 1440: H1 'A water heater that waits for cheap power.' with lede 'a controller an electrician adds to your electric water heater. It holds heating back until your tariff's cheap hours' and 'Join the install list' with 'Installs start in one region; the list opens with it.' A stranger can repeat it. The H1 slightly mis-states the product (it is a controller, not a water heater), corrected one line later.
evidence.fit: Every ask met with a visible resolution: 'Fig. 1 - Example only' day model; no bill saving printed and the caption says 'not a forecast of your bill'; electricians get a four-step install sequence plus wiring sketch and 'Safety listing: in progress, not yet issued'; rebate programmes get an 'Example log - one controller - illustrative values' table plus measured-not-modelled points; unnamed pilot stated; form says it is not connected to a server; 'Check before you join' fit list. Tone is technical and calm, right for electricians and programme managers.
evidence.distinctiveness: Technical-document voice built from the product: 'Fig. 1' mono labels, a chart with tariff band / draws / heater rows / tank-level line with a reserve line, a panel-disconnect-controller-tank wiring sketch (with a stacked version on phones), a per-day switching log for utilities, and a 'Three rules, and the one that overrides the other two' section. You would recognise it without the logo. Condensed sans + serif pairing is the only stock-feeling choice.
evidence.proof: 1440: the example panel is in the first screen with controls and the readout '100% of the heating that would have run at peak price now runs in cheaper hours, in this example.' Operated all 9 tariff x household combinations: numbers stay consistent (totals ~equal, saving shown as shift not kWh), and harder cases show 65-82% with a peak top-up drawn in the chart. Limitation: only preset combinations, the visitor cannot set their own hours or tank.
evidence.craft: Sharp hierarchy: big condensed H1 left, lede and CTA right, figure spanning below; mono figure labels and tabular kWh figures; consistent rule lines. Visible defect: the header 'Join the install list' button at 1440 and 768 renders dark text rgb(21,24,28) on blue #1646c8 (about 2.3:1; axe color-contrast at 1440), unlike the white-text hero button. Desktop segmented controls are 36px tall. Long section headings ('For rebate programmes: a shifted load you can see, without a call to the homeowner') wrap to four lines at 1440.
evidence.mobile: 390: real recomposition. 'Menu' button opens a full-width list (aria-expanded true), tapping 'Installers' closes it and jumps to the section. Segmented tariff/household controls go full width at 107x44 and 108x49. The chart switches to a compact layout with labels above each row, and the wiring sketch swaps to a stacked version. Promise, CTA and Fig. 1 title fit in the first screen. Weak spot: after tapping 'Night rate' the % readout and table are ~700px below the controls, though the chart directly below does update.
evidence.honesty: Example label sits on the figure ('Example only'), table caption says 'from this simple model, not from a meter... not a forecast of your bill'; form note before submit says it sends nothing and success says 'nothing was sent'. Against that: a large blue '100%' stat sits in the first screen at 1440, which reads as a headline claim even with 'in this example' after it, for a client who said he won't print numbers; the lede promises 'showers stay hot' while the model's 'Night rate + Evening showers' case shows 'Draws that ran short: 0 vs 1' with Tankshift, unexplained; 'No subscription is planned' is a commitment the brief did not give.
evidence.interaction: Operated tariff and household radios at 1440/768/390 through all 9 combinations; chart, readout, live status line ('Showing night rate tariff with evening showers: 66%... with 1 peak top-up') all update; details 'Hot-water use in this example, as a list' opens with the draw list; mobile menu opens/closes. Form: empty submit -> 'Enter an email address like name@example.com.', then postcode error, valid submit -> 'Noted and saved on this device... nothing was sent'; reload shows the saved state and refills email. No console errors. Model is preset-only, so there is no empty/edge state to reach in the artifact.
evidence.copy: Specific to the trade: 'takes the feed after the disconnect. One box, one conduit run, no connection inside the tank', 'Force a peak block and confirm the element stays off; force the reserve and confirm it heats', 'A hot shower outranks a cheap one', 'The saving is on price, not on kilowatt-hours'. Buttons say what happens. Weaknesses: some headings run long, and 'showers stay hot' in the lede conflicts with the model's own short-draw case.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific outcome ('holds heating back until your tariff's cheap hours... peak hours stay quiet'), CTA with 'Installs start in one region', and the working example (controls, chart rows, 100% readout) all in one viewport. 390: H1, lede, CTA with the region note and the 'Fig. 1 - Example only / Try a day' heading in view; the chart itself starts just below.

problems: Header 'Join the install list' button has dark text on blue (~2.3:1) at 1440 and 768, a visible contrast defect on the most repeated action

A big '100%' stat leads the readout in the first screen, and the 'Night rate + Evening showers' case shows Tankshift causing a short draw while the lede promises 'showers stay hot'; both sit uneasily with the client's no-unbacked-numbers stance
The day model is preset-only (3 tariffs x 3 households) and on mobile its readout sits ~700px below the controls

reason: B builds its whole page out of the product: the example sits in the first screen at 1440, the phone layout is recomposed, not shrunk, and electricians and rebate programmes each get an artifact of their own (install sequence with wiring sketch, switching log). A has the more hands-on strip and the cleaner honesty, but it holds that idea below a text-only hero, and the rest of the page is a generic stack. If B's 100% stat were judged a printed savings-style claim against the brief, or if direct manipulation of hours mattered more than first-screen proof and audience paths, I would move toward A.
